runs.brief:
# Risk Brief — Compliance & Quality Watch  
**Profile:** Tesla Model Y 2021‑2025 · Chevrolet Bolt EV 2019‑2023 · Hyundai Ioniq 5 2022‑2025 · Volkswagen ID.4 2021‑2025  
**Markets:** NL, EU, UK, US  
**Run date:** 2026‑10‑17  

---

## Executive summary
- **Hyundai Ioniq 5 HV battery cell recall (F406)** published 2026‑07‑02 adds a *new fire-while-parked/driving* risk for 2023‑2024 MY — the most recent high-severity action in the set.  
- **Chevrolet Bolt EV** carries a *triple-layer battery recall stack* (F397, F398, F399) with two re‑repair campaigns; completion rates for the 2024‑10‑31 re‑inspection (F399) are unknown and critical.  
- **Tesla Model Y** has two *active 2025 recalls* covering the current MY range: rear‑view camera loss (F385) and EPS assist loss at stop (F386). Both are FMVSS non‑compliances.  
- **Volkswagen ID.4** door‑handle water ingress (F425, 2021‑2024 MY) and passenger airbag inflator fastener (F433, 2023‑2024 MY) recalls affect all four markets.  
- **Four early‑warning signals** (S1–S3, S4‑VW) show complaint spikes on *software‑driven distraction (Tesla), brake caliper fracture (Chevrolet), steer‑by‑wire loss (Hyundai), and airbag inflator (VW)* — none yet have recalls.  

**This week:**  
1. Obtain Bolt EV battery re‑repair completion data (F399) from GM; escalate if <90 %.  
2. Confirm Tesla F385/F386 remedy availability in EU/UK/NL — both are US‑published only.  
3. Open safety‑defect investigations for Chevrolet brake caliper (S2) and Hyundai EPS (S3) per 49 CFR 573 / EU 2019/2144.  
4. Verify VW ID.4 door‑handle (F425) and inflator (F433) parts supply for NL/EU dealers.  

---

## Top risks
| Severity | Item | Affected | Deadline / timing | Action | Ref |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| High | Chevrolet Bolt EV — HV battery fire (triple recall stack) | 2020‑2022 Bolt EV / EUV; previously repaired under 21V‑650 | Ongoing; 2024‑10‑31 re‑inspection (F399) | Audit dealer completion of F399; request GM field‑fix rate; prepare EU/UK RAPEX if US rate <90 % | [F397][F398][F399] |
| High | Hyundai Ioniq 5 — HV battery cell misaligned electrodes (fire) | 2023‑2024 Ioniq 5 | Recall published 2026‑07‑02 (F406) | Track repair launch; confirm cell‑supplier lot containment; assess 2025 MY exposure | [F406] |
| High | Tesla Model Y — Rear‑view camera image loss (FMVSS 111) | 2021‑2025 Model Y | Recall published 2025‑01‑07 (F385) | Verify OTA/parts fix in NL/EU/UK; check HW4 controller overlap with S1 | [F385] |
| High | Tesla Model Y — EPS assist loss at stop/accel | 2023 Model Y (sw <2023.38.4) | Recall published 2025‑02‑14 (F386) | Confirm software remedy deployed; monitor for 2024‑2025 MY extension | [F386] |
| High | Hyundai Ioniq 5 — Braking software: reduced brake + unintended acceleration (LFB/N e‑shift) | 2025 Ioniq 5 “N” | Recall published 2025‑04‑11 (F409) | Validate OTA rollout completion; test LFB/e‑shift inhibition logic | [F409] |
| High | Hyundai Ioniq 5 — Rear suspension fastener loosening (loss of control) | 2025 Ioniq 5 | Recall published 2026‑05‑19 (F415) | Inspect dealer repair rate; check fastener supplier lot traceability | [F415] |
| High | Volkswagen ID.4 — Door handle water ingress → unexpected opening | 2021‑2024 ID.4 (NL, EU, UK, US) | Recall published 2024‑09‑04 (F425) | Confirm parts availability in NL/EU; monitor for 2025 MY extension | [F425] |
| High | Volkswagen ID.4 — Passenger airbag inflator fasteners loose | 2023‑2024 ID.4 (NL, EU, UK, US) | Recall published 2024‑08‑28 (F433) | Audit dealer torque‑check completion; verify inflator supplier corrective action | [F433] |
| High | Chevrolet Bolt EV — Front brake caliper anti‑click washer fracture (brake drag, 628 °F, fire/crash) | 2017‑2020 Bolt EV (signal scope) | **No recall yet**; 90‑day spike 6× baseline | Issue TSB for washer/caliper inspection; audit harness heat damage; prepare recall if fracture rate > threshold | [S2] |
| High | Hyundai Ioniq 5 — Intermittent EPS/steer‑by‑wire assist loss (loss of control at speed, injury crash) | 2022‑2025 Ioniq 5 (signal scope) | **No recall yet**; 90‑day spike 1.6× baseline, 2 loss‑of‑control events | Pull EPS ECU logs from 4 VINs; correlate DAW/CAN timestamps; open SDI; tow‑if‑warning TSB | [S3] |

*Only 10 rows shown; additional High recalls exist (e.g., Bolt EV seat‑belt bolts F396, airbag fasteners F400/F401; VW rear‑view camera chain F427‑F429, motor seal F430, cable routing F431, sunshade F432) — track in backlog.*

---

## Early‑warning signals
| Signal | Vehicle / Component | Spike | Key failure mode | Safety verdict | Evidence strength | Immediate OEM steps |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **S1** | Tesla Model Y — Electrical / Infotainment OTA | 1.5× (3 vs 1.97/90d) | Mandatory non‑dismissing feedback overlay on every FSD disengagement obscures ⅓ of center display (nav, parking camera) at takeover moment | **Acute distraction / crash risk** — design guarantees obstruction during high‑workload transition | Moderate — 2 identical owner reports + 1 HW4 chain report; reproducible UI behavior | 1. Emergency OTA: make overlay non‑modal / auto‑dismiss ≤5 s / defer until Park. 2. Cross‑check HW4 failures (complaint 2) for shared controller. 3. NHTSA Phase‑2 distraction review. 4. Recall if zero‑obstruction not provable. |
| **S2** | Chevrolet Bolt EV — Service Brakes | 6.0× (3 vs 0.49/90d) | Anti‑rattle washer fracture → pad misalignment → extreme heat (628 °F), steering wobble, wiring melt, regen‑brake faults | **Crash & fire risk** — sudden directional control loss, wheel‑end fire, propulsion loss | Moderate‑strong — 3 complaints, one with thermal data, one with OnStar alert; all same hardware | 1. TSB: inspect/replace anti‑click washers & caliper hardware 2017‑2020. 2. Audit harness routing near front brakes. 3. Validate regen‑brake thermal logic. 4. Prepare recall if fracture rate exceeds threshold. |
| **S3** | Hyundai Ioniq 5 — Steering (EPS) | 1.6× (4 vs 2.47/90d) | EPS motor/ECU or torque‑sensor dropout → abrupt assist loss; CAN glitch → simultaneous brake‑by‑wire inhibition; transient self‑clearing faults | **High crash/injury risk** — total steering+braking loss at 70 mph; 30+ mph barrier impact w/o airbag deploy | Moderate — 4 reports, 2 independent loss‑of‑control events, 1 injury crash; intermittent, non‑reproducible at dealer | 1. Pull EPS ECU flash logs & gateway CAN traces (OTA/dealer). 2. Correlate DAW/IR timestamps with EPS dropouts. 3. Audit EPS motor/ECU supplier lots for torque‑sensor solder voids. 4. TSB: “Check DAW + steering warning → do not drive; tow for EPS ECU replacement.” 5. Open SDI per 49 CFR 573. |
| **S4 (VW)** | Volkswagen ID.4 — Airbags | 1.5× (3 vs 1.97/90d) | *Signal content not provided in feed* — only header present | **Unknown** — cannot assess without complaint narratives | **Thin** — baseline and multiplier only; no failure mode or injury data | Request full complaint narratives from NHTSA/ODI; cross‑check with inflator fastener recall F433 (2023‑2024 MY) for common supplier. |

---

## Watch next (90 days)
| Vehicle | Watch item | Trigger / threshold | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Chevrolet Bolt EV** | Battery re‑repair (F399) completion rate | <90 % by 2026‑11‑15 → escalate to EU/UK RAPEX | Compliance |
| **Chevrolet Bolt EV** | Brake caliper washer fracture rate (S2) | ≥5 confirmed fractures in 2017‑2020 MY → open recall prep | Quality |
| **Hyundai Ioniq 5** | Ioniq 5 battery cell recall (F406) launch in EU/UK/NL | No VIN‑level remedy notice by 2026‑11‑01 → formal KBA/RDW inquiry | Compliance |
| **Hyundai Ioniq 5** | EPS steer‑by‑wire SDI (S3) | Root cause confirmed in ≥3 VINs → recall decision | Safety |
| **Tesla Model Y** | F385/F386 remedy in NL/EU/UK | No dealer/OTA fix by 2026‑11‑15 → notify RDW/KBA/DVSA | Compliance |
| **Tesla Model Y** | OTA overlay distraction (S1) | NHTSA ODI opened or ≥5 similar complaints → recall push | Safety |
| **Volkswagen ID.4** | Door handle (F425) & inflator (F433) parts supply NL/EU | Dealer stock‑out >14 days → escalate to VW Group logistics | Quality |
| **Volkswagen ID.4** | Airbag inflator complaint detail (S4‑VW) | Full narratives received → link to F433 supplier lot | Safety |
| **All** | Semiconductor / HV cell supplier alerts | Any Tier‑1 supplier quality alert (LGES, CATL, SK On, Panasonic, etc.) → immediate BOM trace | Supply Chain |

---  
*End of brief. All citations refer to supplied findings [F###] and signals [S#]. Evidence gaps noted where signal narratives are missing.*

**Verdict: Post-OTA persistent "Why did you intervene?" modal blocks ~⅓ of center display—including navigation and parking camera—at the exact moment a driver must assume control from FSD, creating acute distraction and crash risk.**

**Common failure mode**  
A 2026 over-the-air update introduced a mandatory, non-dismissing feedback overlay that triggers on every FSD disengagement. It remains until the driver taps a button or shifts to Park, obscuring critical controls and camera views precisely when the system has just failed to handle the driving task.

**Safety risk**  
Crash: driver attention is diverted to a menu during high-workload takeover events; navigation, media, and rear-camera visibility are partially masked. No injuries/fires reported yet, but the design guarantees distraction at the worst possible instant.

**Evidence strength**  
Moderate. Two independent owners describe identical UI behavior post-update; a third reports a cascading HW4/low-voltage hardware failure chain that may share the same central computer. Spike is only 1.5× baseline (3 vs. 1.97/90 days), but the hazard pattern is clear and reproducible.

**OEM immediate actions**  
1. Push emergency OTA: make overlay non-modal, auto-dismiss after 5 s, or defer until vehicle stopped.  
2. Verify whether HW4 failures (complaint 2) involve the infotainment/autonomy controller running this prompt.  
3. Run distraction-guideline review (NHTSA Phase 2) and document mitigation for regulators.  
4. If software fix cannot guarantee zero obstruction during takeover, open a safety recall.

**Verdict: Anti-click washer fracture causes brake drag, extreme wheel overheating (628°F), violent steering wobble, and regenerative-braking electrical faults — crash and fire risk.**

**Failure mode:** The anti-rattle (anti-click) washer on the front brake caliper fractures, allowing pad misalignment and continuous drag. This generates extreme localized heat (627.9°F vs. <200°F other wheels), steering oscillation, burning odor, and can melt adjacent wiring harnesses, triggering regenerative-braking alerts and propulsion loss.

**Safety risk:** Sudden loss of directional control (steering wobble), potential wheel-end fire, and regenerative-braking failure leading to unexpected deceleration or no-brake conditions. Crash and fire potential high.

**Evidence strength:** Moderate–strong. 3 complaints (6× baseline), one with quantified thermal data, one citing a known-design blog, one with OnStar regenerative-braking alert. All point to same hardware.

**OEM actions now:** 1) Issue TSB to inspect/replace anti-click washers and caliper hardware on 2017–2020 Bolt EVs. 2) Audit harness routing near front brakes for heat damage. 3) Validate regenerative-braking fault logic for thermal false-positives. 4) Prepare safety recall if fracture rate exceeds threshold.

**VERDICT: Probable intermittent Electric Power Steering (EPS) / steer-by-wire fault causing sudden assist loss, DAW-system interaction, and alignment drift; crash & injury risk high.**

**Failure Modes**  
- EPS motor/ECU or torque-sensor dropout → abrupt loss of power assist (Complaints 1, 2).  
- CAN/ethernet bus glitch triggering “Check DAW” warning and simultaneous brake-by-wire inhibition (Complaint 1).  
- Transient software fault self-clears before dealer scan (Complaint 2).  
- Persistent toe/camber shift from EPS calibration drift or rack mechanical wear (Complaint 4).

**Safety Risk**  
- **Crash**: Total steering+braking loss at 70 mph (Complaint 1); uncontrolled acceleration into fixed object (Complaint 3).  
- **Injury**: Driver chest trauma from steering wheel; airbags did not deploy in 30+ mph barrier impact (Complaint 3).  
- **Fire**: Not reported, but EPS high-voltage harness fault possible.

**Evidence Strength**  
- 4 reports vs 2.47 baseline (1.6× spike).  
- Two independent loss-of-control events at speed + one injury crash.  
- Intermittent, non-reproducible at dealer → typical of electronic steering faults.  
- DAW warning linkage suggests software/common-bus root cause.

**OEM Immediate Actions**  
1. Pull EPS ECU flash logs & gateway CAN traces from all four VINs (OTA or dealer pull).  
2. Correlate DAW-camera/IR sensor timestamps with EPS torque-sensor dropouts.  
3. Audit EPS motor/ECU supplier lot codes; check for torque-sensor solder voids.  
4. Issue TSB: “If ‘Check DAW’ + steering warning → do not drive; tow to dealer for EPS ECU replacement.”  
5. Open Safety Defect Investigation (SDI) per 49 CFR 573; prepare recall if root cause confirmed in ≥3 vehicles.
